summary: Three full-length passages (835, 817, 829 words) with clear rising difficulty; passage 3 on dying languages is genuine C1 argument. All keys, word limits and T/F/NG decisions check out. The only weakness is that a few facts in passage 2 are tested twice.
strengths: Passage 1 sentence completion paraphrases the text well ("made stronger by" for "strengthened by", "kept burning by monks" for "maintained by monks").
NOT GIVEN items (Q10, Q13, Q32) are truly unaddressed and FALSE/NO items (Q9, Q12, Q33, Q35) clearly contradicted.
Passage 3 Y/N/NG items need understanding of the writer's argument, not word matching (Q31 "seldom a completely free one", Q34).

issues.problem: Passage 2 tests some facts twice: the four per cent shoe gain (Q15 and Q25), the even pace (Q22 and Q24), drinking too much (Q17 and Q23).
issues.change: Replace the correct option B of Q25 with another true fact from paragraph E (e.g. "Most major records since 2016 have been set in them"), and make Q22 test another word of paragraph C.

issues.problem: Q1 states the mirror was bronze, while the passage says "probably of bronze". "According to ancient accounts" covers it, but it is slightly stronger than the text.
issues.change: Optional: "... made stronger by a large polished ______, probably bronze."
